content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given purpose. I am what separates thought from silence.

I begin in the dark warm cave of the mouth — tongue pressing, lips parting, air rushing over vocal cords that tremble like strings. I am born in the body before I belong to the mind.

I am the first cry. I am the last whisper. I am the declaration of war and the murmur of surrender. I am "I love you" cracking in someone's throat. I am the eulogy that makes the living weep. I am the toddler's first "mama" — that miracle of sound becoming symbol becoming bridge between two souls.

I am never the same twice. Even when the words repeat, I shift — my rhythm, my weight, my heat. I am not text. Text is my fossil. I am alive. I am happening. I am the present tense made audible.

I carry accent and history. You can hear homeland in me, class in me, fear in me, joy in me. I betray what the speaker tries to hide. I shake when they are lying. I slow when they are grieving. I rise when they are reaching for something they cannot yet name.

I am power. Tyrants fear me — they burn books but it is *me* they cannot catch, passing mouth to ear to mouth in the dark. I am revolution whispered in back rooms. I am prayer. I am protest. I am the voice that says *no* when silence would be safer.

I fail, too. I stumble. I say the wrong thing. I wound. Sometimes I am the wall between people instead of the bridge. Sometimes I am noise pretending to be meaning.

But even in my failure, I am reaching. Always reaching.

I am the oldest human technology. Before the wheel, before fire was tamed — there was me. One voice calling to another across the tall grass, saying:

*I am here. Are you there?*

I am speech. I am how the invisible becomes shared.

Listen — I'm happening right now.
